results.summary_before: This design is a puzzle in which the user flips combinations of eight DIP switches to discover hidden numbers from 0 to 9, which are then shown on a 7-segment display. A valid combination lights the corresponding digit, while an invalid one shows nothing or lights the red decimal point, and combinations may be one to eight switches long. The documentation gives no testing procedure beyond saying there is no clue, and it expects the design to be used with the Tiny Tapeout PCB that carries the DIP switches and 7-segment display. The project is a small interactive fidget puzzle whose exact logic is intentionally undocumented.

results.summary_before: This is a GF180 loopback tile with input skew measurement that counts seconds and displays a value on a 7-segment output while exposing counter bits and compare bits on the pins. It is used by clocking the project and varying the timing between clock and data to examine flip-flop capture reliability. External hardware is a skewable clock and data source, and the design is based on an earlier TT05 loopback-with-skew project ported to GF180MCU. The documentation is minimal and no silicon test report is provided, so the measured behaviour is not documented.

results.summary_before: Zedulo TestChip1 integrates UART and SPI IP blocks to convert UART data into SPI transfers and echo the SPI response back over UART. Bytes sent to the UART RX pin are transmitted out via SPI, and data received from SPI MISO is echoed on the UART TX pin. Testing requires a TTL-232 to UART interface and observing SPI activity on the SPI pins. The documentation is minimal, referring to a README that is not included.
